what: Two-panel training-dynamics view of the final CCP configuration (v7 head=220, arm s1, a2wt1, 6000 steps). (a) optimised objective with its chain and slot components, log scale; (b) clipped gradient norm (left log axis) against the slot-head bias g_pos and the held-out operator top-1 accuracy (right axis).
one_line_reading: The objective falls 4.03 -> 0.025 nats over 6000 steps and the clipped gradient norm decays 98 -> 1.9 with it; the two held-out accuracies on the right axis are inert (operator top-1 is saturated at 1.00 from step 50, g_pos stays near 0.37), so this run must be read off the loss, not off eval.
method: loss/chain/slot/text taken verbatim from the jsonl; curves drawn as 51-step centred moving average over the raw trace; eval points are the rotating 48-row held-out pool evaluated every 50 steps.
caveats: 'text' (render-token CE, ~7-8 nats) uses a different denominator than loss/chain/slot and is kept only in the CSV.

eval_sel_top1 is 1.00 already at step 50 and exactly 1.00 at 86 of the 120 eval points -- a saturated / too-easy probe that must NOT be presented as a learning curve. Its residual variance is n_frames rounding.

eval_slot_top1 decays to 0.0 by step 6000 (from 0.400 at step 50) even though the slot training loss falls to 0.019 -- the two slot read-outs disagree; eval_render_tok_acc stays flat at 0.26-0.31. Neither is quoted in the panel.
the eval pool rotates (eval_rotate), so successive eval points are not on an identical row set.
